baer-heitev/1:_: From one to another. And all the more so if the shamash went out, one may not kindle from a Hanukkah light. Maharshal wrote that in the synagogue there is no distinction between the shamash and the other lights, for all the lights inside are called a mitzvah light; therefore one should rebuke those who kindle their lights by maidservants from a synagogue light, except on Motzei Shabbat because of the dark alleyways through which Saul merited the kingdom. A havdalah light is called a mitzvah light; but after one has made havdalah on it the mitzvah is already done and one may kindle from it, for even a Hanukkah light after its required time is no longer called a mitzvah light — end quote; see siman 554.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] [Levush] If the wind extinguished it, etc. So wrote Terumat HaDeshen, and the Taz wondered: if so, from light to light as well — why is it permitted even when moving a light that one wishes to kindle to a light from which one is kindling, and one must in any case leave it in its place as written in siman 675 — until here. In my humble opinion there is no difficulty, for even at the end of siman 675, if one holds it a short time and then places it, he has fulfilled; if so, since kindling accomplishes the mitzvah, even if it went out before he placed it, nevertheless when he returns and kindles it and leaves it a short time until half an hour passes, together with the first kindling he has fulfilled. It also appears to me that according to what the Levush explained the Gemara meaning of kindling from light to light — that one takes a burning light to a placed light and kindles it from it.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (5) In Hanukkah lights, etc. — and specifically in Hanukkah lights for the reason explained below; but in other mitzvah lights such as Shabbat lights and synagogue lights and the like, one kindles from light to light [Darkei Moshe]. So agreed Chamed Moshe, for such is the practice of the world; so too in Chayei Adam; and so it is implied above in siman 554 seif 14, that specifically a layman's light may not be kindled from a synagogue light, but light from light is permitted, and the Rama did not emend there at all to be stringent — it is obvious to him that in this there is no custom to be stringent. See Peri Megadim: by a weekday light it is not worthwhile even for other mitzvah lights. See below what we write on this.
